title: Build request
description: What a person actually asks for: these cores, for this subtopic, for this learner, with these purposes. It is the production input the repository never had -- every gate below it could refuse bad content, and nothing could say which rung to start at or whether transfer is even wanted. It is not a library record and reaches no learner.

label.description: What a person calls this request.

cores.description: Which products are wanted. Asking for a product is not the same as the system agreeing to produce it: a purpose may withhold one, and an absent rung blocks one.

learner.description: Where the entry rung comes from. Exactly one of three, because a percentage typed into a field is a decision and this makes saying so unavoidable.

profile_ref.description: A profile in Learners/profiles. The entry rung is selected from its per-capability map, never from its knowledge_percentage.

owner_entry.description: An owner naming the entry rung outright. The shortest honest path when no diagnostic exists.

owner_estimate.description: The percentage a person types, recorded as what it is. It selects an entry rung and may never be read as evidence that a prerequisite is held.

practice.description: What each practice run is for. A purpose carries its own support level, so the practice cores need no knowledge number at all -- these are separate questions and were previously one.
